links.outcome: Segmentation quality across normal versus pathological aortic anatomy categories
links.effect: Quality varied by category (p<0.001): best in young patients (median 5), poorest in dissections (median 3) and aneurysms (median 4); overall median 4, 77% good or excellent.
links.quote: Performance was consistent across segments (p = 0.16) but varied by category (p < 0.001): best in young patients (5 [IQR 4-5]) and adequate in non-contrast and venous-phase scans (4 [IQR 4-5]), poorest in dissections (3 [IQR 3-4]) and aneurysms (4 [IQR 3-4]).

screen.reason: The study conducts a clinical stress-test evaluating the boundaries and failure modes of an existing off-the-shelf AI segmentation tool (TotalSegmentator-AI) across normal and pathological aortic CT scans, but does not test an intervention or deployment safeguard practice.
